rows.annotation: DUF3422 family inner membrane protein of unknown molecular function.
rows.evidence: The query has a DUF3422 match covering 98.8% of its sequence (E=4.9e-115) and two predicted transmembrane helices at residues 345–365 and 380–397. A 93.8%-identity STRING homolog belongs to COG4949, an uncharacterized membrane-anchored family. Distant homologs show strong fitness defects on L-proline, L-citrulline, L-ornithine or D-xylose, without establishing a shared molecular activity. Conservation spans 18 other organisms at 30.1–76.6% identity.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is met by the explicit criterion of substrate-specific fitness phenotypes, although these occur in distant homologs and do not resolve the query's molecular function. Query domain and topology predictions converge with STRING family evidence on a DUF3422 membrane protein; manuscript summaries, moderate cofitness and variable neighborhoods provide no biochemical assignment. A proline transporter annotation is unsupported because the fitness phenotypes span different substrates across organisms and no characterized homolog or transport-specific domain establishes transport activity.

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 18 (in 15 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 18 (14 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 30.1-76.6
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
